newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end off best levels after weak GDP data.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end off best levels after weak GDP data.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up Wednesday as some local investors finally came off the sidelines to hunt for bargains after weeks of watching prices slip, brokers said.

But after investors were disappointed by the latest gross domestic product (GDP) figure -- announced by the government late in the session -- earlier price gains were shaved toward the close, they added.
Due to the economy's slower-than-expected growth, the market is seen falling back Thursday and a short-term recovery is also unlikely, they said.

In the first nine months of the year, the economy grew 1.9 percent, compared to 8.9 percent in the same period of 1995, while the GDP September year-on-year rise was 0.4 percent, compared with 3.9 percent year-on-year growth in the same month last year, according to the government.
While poor third quarter earnings had prepared investors for a low September GDP figure, they had not expected such weak growth, brokers said.
"The GDP figures are really poor and will definitely not please investors," said Luis Calderon of local brokerage Accval.
Wednesday, the General Index .IGRA rose 0.79 percent to 1,485.4 points, and the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL rose 1.33 percent to 2,066.9 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
Due to rules introduced on the market this week, stocks can continue to be traded, but their prices are fixed one hour before the end of the day's session at 1700 local time/2200 GMT.
Brokers and stock exchange officials have said the market's indices will only vary slightly in this final hour.
Wednesday's volume at the time prices were fixed was estimated at a meager 25.0 million soles ($9.7 million), brokers said.

Benchmark Telefnica del Per rose 0.74 percent to 5.45 soles, on a preliminary count of 1.251 million shares. Among other leaders, Credicorp Ltd rose 3.22 percent to $17.65 on a preliminary share total of 166,035. Tin-miner Minsur climbed 0.35 percent to 23.07 soles on a preliminary share count of 70,060.
